methods.today: Generative Remove as it ships: the spot filled from the photo as the reference, prompt remove, four steps, seed 0
methods.a: RM-20 A: today's fill, then its upsampled latents noised to 0.8 and run through 0.4 to 0 in full-size tiles of 1024 pixels overlapping by 128, no reference
methods.b: RM-20 B: today's fill, then detail transfer (research/prototypes/generative/detail_transfer.py), stored without added noise
methods.ref-softened: RM-21: the reference blurred inside the spot
methods.ref-generated: RM-21: the reference filled by the model itself at half resolution, without a reference
methods.context-wider: RM-21: the crop up to four times the spot's size at the same level (at most 1024 pixels)
methods.context-coarser: RM-21: the crop four times the spot's size, on a coarser level when that's what fits
methods.steps-8: RM-21: eight steps instead of four
methods.b-s1.2: RM-20 B with the low-pass at 1.2 coarse texels instead of 0.6
methods.b-s2.0: RM-20 B with the low-pass at 2 coarse texels instead of 0.6

scores: research/prototypes/generative/score_removal.py: sharpness (band energy less the noise model's, spot over ring, per band), noise (spot and ring over the noise model), seam (gradient across the edge over 10 to 16 pixels outside), and for composites PSNR and low-pass PSNR against the truth in the square root of linear camera RGB
notes: One seed (0) for every generative fill. Times are each fill's own in seconds (a run's whole time when it made no fill), under the load average given: two other agents shared the Mac and its GPU, so none is a quiet measurement. B's transfer times are the Python prototype's. peakRSS_GB is the CLI's resident memory, which doesn't count all of MLX's buffers. The composites' truth is scored from the same spot's areas on the truth DNG.
